candidates.description: The maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of the primary or recurrent pulmonary nodule/mass, representing its metabolic activity on FDG-PET/CT.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the SUVmax value associated with the pulmonary nodule or mass (e.g., 'SUVmax ≈ 8.5' or 'SUVmax = 12.0').
candidates.measurement_definition: Numeric SUVmax value as reported in the PET/CT findings for the pulmonary lesion.
candidates.name: pulmonary_lesion_suvmax
candidates.uncertainty: Variability in SUVmax may be influenced by the uptake time and glucose levels, though these are generally standardized across the reports.

citations.quote: New lytic lesions with intense FDG avidity identified in the body of T5 (SUVmax ≈ 6.8) and the posterior element of T7 (SUVmax ≈ 6.4)
No focal FDG‑avid osseous lesions identified throughout the visualized axial and appendicular skeleton. No evidence of metastatic bone disease.
Multiple focal FDG‑avid lesions identified: - T4 vertebral body (SUVmax 6.1) - T6 vertebral body (SUVmax 5.8) - T8 vertebral body (SUVmax 6.3) - T10 vertebral body (SUVmax 5.5)

candidates.description: Presence of metastatic disease in the skeletal system, characterized by lytic, sclerotic, or FDG-avid lesions in the vertebrae, ribs, or pelvis.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Assign positive if findings describe 'lytic lesions', 'osteoblastic lesions', or 'FDG-avid osseous lesions' in the skeleton. Assign negative if reports state 'No focal FDG‑avid osseous lesions' or 'No evidence of metastatic bone disease'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if the report identifies any focal osseous lesions suggestive of metastasis; negative if the report explicitly states no focal osseous lesions or no evidence of metastatic bone disease.
candidates.name: osseous_metastasis
candidates.uncertainty: Whether mild FDG uptake in the absence of CT-defined lytic/sclerotic changes is consistently interpreted as metastasis across all reports.

limitations: The evidence is restricted to radiology reports, which may lack full clinical context regarding the timing of the baseline measurements relative to therapy.
Small sample size of patients in the provided excerpts may not represent the full heterogeneity of NSCLC presentations.
summary: The evidence identifies key imaging features in patients with recurrent or progressive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), specifically highlighting the metabolic activity of pulmonary nodules and the presence of skeletal metastases as primary clinical distinctions.
